sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: This visa stream lets people who are sponsored, usually by a family member, come to Australia to visit their family members.

sections.heading: Overview > You must
sections.text:
- have a sponsor
- intend to come to Australia as a visitor only.

Help with your visa

If you are getting help with your visa, before you pay someone, read information on Who can help with your visa application.

sections.heading: Overview > With this visa you can
sections.text:
- visit family or friends
- cruise or have a holiday
- study or train for up to 3 months.

You should check if a Visitor (subclass 600) visa in the Tourist stream might better suit you. The Visitor visa (subclass 600) in the Tourist stream also lets you holiday in Australia to see family and friends and does not require a sponsor.

sections.heading: Overview > Cost
sections.text:
(concessions apply in limited circumstances). We might ask your sponsor to pay a security bond.

Cost concession

From 1 July 2026, a lower visa cost applies to eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste citizens who lodge a valid visa application. See About this visa.

To work out what your visa will cost, use the Visa Pricing Estimator. The estimator does not take into account the other costs.

sections.heading: Overview > Processing time
sections.text: For an indication of processing times for this visa, use the visa processing time guide tool. This will show the processing times for recently decided applications. It is a guide only and not specific to your application.

sections.heading: About this visa > With this visa you can
sections.text:
- Visit family or friends
- be here as a tourist, for a cruise or for any purpose except business or medical treatment.

You can study or train for up to 3 months on this visa. But if your main reason for travelling to Australia is study, a student visa might be more appropriate.

You cannot work.

You should check if a Visitor (subclass 600) visa in the Tourist stream might better suit you. The Visitor visa (subclass 600) Tourist stream also lets you holiday in Australia to visit family and friends and does not require a sponsor.

Cruise

You will need a visa if you enter Australia during a cruise.

If your cruise is a round trip cruise, the time you spend on the cruise counts as time spent in Australia - that is, we do not consider you have left Australia. A round trip cruise will not reset your stay period on your visa.

Ask your cruise operator or travel agent if we consider your cruise to be a round trip cruise.

sections.heading: About this visa > How long you can stay
sections.text:
This is a temporary visa.

The standard length of stay for this visa is 3 months. We may grant a stay of up to 12 months in limited circumstances. We determine the length of your visa on a case-by-case basis. Things we might consider when determining your stay period include:

- how long you want to stay
- why you want to stay in Australia.

You might not be granted the length of stay you want.

Generally we grant this visa with only a single entry permitted and with a 6 month validity period. This means that you have up to 6 months after the grant date to enter Australia. If you leave Australia, you need to apply for another visa before you can return.

sections.heading: About this visa > Stay longer
sections.text:
You cannot stay longer in Australia by extending this visa. You must apply for another visa.

You cannot apply for a new visa in Australia because your visa will have condition 8503, 'No Further Stay'. We can waive a no further stay condition in limited circumstances. You must not breach condition 8531. That is, you must not remain in Australia beyond your visa period.

You can explore your visa options.

sections.heading: About this visa > Include family
sections.text:
You cannot include family members in your application. Each family member, including those listed on your passport, must submit a separate application.

If other family members are applying for this visa, you can tell us you are travelling as a group in your application form. See the information about group applications in the Apply for the visa section on the Step by step tab.

We assess each application based on the individual circumstances of the applicant.

Newborn child

Find out what to do if your child is born after you apply.

sections.heading: About this visa > Cost
sections.text:
This visa costs for each applicant (concessions apply in limited circumstances).

You might also have to pay other costs for:

- health checks
- police certificates
- biometrics.

Use the Visa Pricing Estimator to work out what your visa will cost. The estimator does not take into account the other costs.

Cost concession for eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste Visitor visa applicants

From 1 July 2026, a lower visa cost applies to eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste citizens who lodge a valid visa application.

We will charge eligible applicants the lower visa application cost during the application process in ImmiAccount. We will recognise eligible applicants by the valid passport from the specified countries used in the application when they apply.

The applicant must hold a valid passport issued by one of the following countries:

- Federated States of Micronesia
- Fiji
- Kiribati
- Nauru
- Palau
- Papua New Guinea
- Republic of the Marshall Islands
- Samoa
- Solomon Islands
- Timor-Leste
- Tonga
- Tuvalu
- Vanuatu.

sections.heading: About this visa > Apply from
sections.text: To be eligible for this visa, you must be outside Australia when you apply and when we decide on your application.

sections.heading: About this visa > Your obligations
sections.text:
You must meet all visa conditions and obey Australian laws.

Learn more about visa conditions.

sections.heading: About this visa > Health insurance
sections.text:
You are liable for all your healthcare costs while you are in Australia. Insurance can help limit your financial liability. To cover any unexpected medical treatment you might need in Australia, we strongly recommend you take out adequate health insurance.

Learn more about health insurance for overseas visitors.

Some countries have a reciprocal healthcare agreement with Australia. Find out more from Services Australia about reciprocal healthcare agreements.

sections.heading: About this visa > Travel
sections.text:
Generally, we grant this visa with a single entry. A single-entry visa allows you to enter Australia once. You cannot re-enter on the visa. You must apply for another visa to come back.

You should check if a Visitor (subclass 600) visa in the Tourist stream is more suitable for you.

If we grant you a multiple-entry visa, you can travel outside Australia and return as many times as you want while the visa is valid. Check if you have multiple or single entry in Visa Entitlement Verification Online (VEVO) or your visa grant letter.

sections.heading: About this visa > Visa record
sections.text: We will digitally link your visa to your passport. You will not get a label in your passport.

sections.heading: Eligibility
sections.text: You must meet all of these criteria to be eligible for the Visitor visa Family sponsored stream.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet our health requirement
sections.text: You and any family members who apply for the visa with you must meet our health requirement.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet our character requirement
sections.text:
You must meet our character requirement.

We might expect other family members to meet the requirement.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Pay your debts to the Australian Government
sections.text: If you or any family members (including those who don't apply for the visa with you) owe the Australian Government money, you or they must have paid it back or arranged to pay it back.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have enough money
sections.text: You must have, or have access to, enough money to support yourself while you are in Australia.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Be a genuine visitor
sections.text:
You must intend to:

- stay temporarily in Australia
- obey any condition and stay period attached to your visa.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have a sponsor
sections.text:
You must have a sponsor.

To learn about who can sponsor you, see the Sponsor Eligibility tab.

You must provide evidence to prove your relationship with your sponsor. See information about 'Sponsorship documents' in the Gather your documents section of the Step by step tab.

If a family member wants to support you without becoming a sponsor, you can apply for a Visitor visa (subclass 600) in the Tourist stream. Provide a letter of invitation from your family member with your application.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Best interests of the child
sections.text: We might not grant this visa if it is not in the best interests of an applicant under 18.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > Organise health exams
sections.text:
You can complete your health examinations before you apply or you can wait until we tell you to have them.

Find out the examinations you need and how to arrange them if you want to have them before you apply.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > Get help with your application
sections.text:
Only some people can help you with your application. If you appoint someone to give you immigration assistance they must be:

- a registered migration agent
- a legal practitioner, or
- an exempt person.

You can appoint anyone to receive documents on your behalf relating to your visa matter.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Provide accurate information
sections.text:
Provide accurate information.

See what happens if you can't prove your identity or don't provide true information.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Identity documents
sections.text:
Provide the pages of your current passport showing your photo, personal details and passport issue and expiry dates.

Also provide:

- a national identity card, if you have one
- proof of change of name, if applicable, such as:

- a marriage or divorce certificate
- change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority
- documents that show other names you have been known by

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Genuine visitor documents
sections.text:
Provide as much proof as you can to show you are visiting Australia as a temporary visitor only. This could include:

- proof you have enough money for your stay and to leave Australia, such as personal bank statements, pay slips, audited accounts, tax records or credit card limit.
- a letter from your relative or friend in Australia, inviting you to visit. The letter could state:

- their relationship to you
- the purpose of your visit and length of stay
- if you will be staying with them. If this person will be paying for your stay, provide proof of their funds

- your plans while in Australia

Proof that you have reasons to return home such as:

- a letter from your employer stating you plan to return to your job
- proof that you study at a school, college or university in your home country
- proof that you have immediate family members in your home country
- proof that you can return home
- proof that you own a house or other major assets in your home country

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Sponsorship documents
sections.text:
Your sponsor must complete Form 1149 - Application for sponsorship for Sponsored Family Visitors (329KB PDF). Provide a copy of the completed form with your application.

You need to provide documents with your application to prove the relationship between each applicant and your sponsor. This can include:

- birth certificates
- passport pages showing names of parents
- family register
- marriage certificates.

Example

If your aunt is sponsoring you, you need to attach a document or a set of documents, which collectively prove the relationship. Documents can include the family register or the set of birth certificates for you, your parent and your aunt.

If you cannot provide documents to prove your relationship, you can apply for a Visitor (subclass 600) visa in the Tourist stream. You can attach a letter of invitation or support from your family member with your application.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Character documents
sections.text: Provide any military service record or discharge papers, if applicable.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Additional documents for applicants under 18
sections.text:
You must get consent for any applicant under 18 years of age to migrate to Australia from anyone who:

- has a legal right to decide where the child lives and
- is not coming to Australia with the child

They must complete either:

- Form 1229 Consent form to grant an Australian visa to a child under the age of 18 years
- a statutory declaration giving their consent for the child to visit Australia on this visa

Alternatively, you can show us:

- an Australian court order that allows your child to migrate to Australia, or
- that the laws of your home country allow them to migrate

Include:

- an identity document that shows the signature and photo of the person who completed the form or declaration, such as a passport or driver’s licence
- adoption papers or other court documents if applicable

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Tell us you are getting help
sections.text:
To nominate someone to:

- receive your correspondence, use Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- provide immigration assistance, use Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.

Upload your written notification or your forms to ImmiAccount.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Translate
sections.text:
Have all non-English documents translated into English.

Provide original and translated documents in your application.

Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters.

Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited. But on each translation, they must include their:

- full name
- address and telephone number
- qualifications and experience in the language they are translating

These details must be in English.

Note: You don't need to have any documents certified.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Scan or photograph
sections.text:
Scan or photograph all documents (English and non-English) in colour.

The scans and photos must be clear and legible.

If a document is more than one page, save it all as one file.

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa > Provide accurate information
sections.text: See what happens if you cannot prove your identity or don't provide true information.

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa > Group applications
sections.text:
Some visa applications allow two or more applicants travelling together as a group to have their separate applications processed together.

One applicant should create the group to generate a group ID. The other applicants should then include that group ID in their applications.

Applicants may create a group on the ‘Manage groups’ tab in ImmiAccount. Applications that allow for group processing will ask about this on the second page.

Applicants should be aware that generally, we will process the applications together. We process each application in the group on its own merits.

Apply online

- Log in or create an ImmiAccount.
- Attach documents.
- Pay the application fee. We will not process your application until you pay the fee.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply
sections.text:
We will let you know when we have received your application and documents.

There are other things you need to know and might need to do.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Biometrics
sections.text: We will let you know if you need to provide biometrics.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Health exams
sections.text: If you didn't have health exams before you applied for the visa, have them if we tell you to.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Send more information
sections.text:
If you did not send us all documents when you applied, send them via ImmiAccount as soon as you can.

We might also ask you to provide more information.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Mistakes on your application
sections.text:
Let us know as soon as you can if you made a mistake on your application.

Complete Form 1023 Notification of incorrect answers.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Help with your application
sections.text:
Let us know if you no longer want someone to:

- receive your correspondence - complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- provide immigration advice - complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.

Upload your written notification or your forms to ImmiAccount.

For more information see Who can help you with your application.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Tell us if things change
sections.text:
Tell us if things change after you lodge your application but before we have made a decision.

Things you need to let us know about include:

- you want to withdraw your application
- changes to your phone number, address or passport
- changes to your relationship status
- the birth of a child

sections.heading: Step by step > Visa outcome
sections.text:
We will let you know our decision on your visa application in writing. We will tell you:

- your visa grant number
- the date your visa starts
- your visa conditions.

Keep a copy of our decision with you when in Australia.

If we refuse your visa we will let you know in writing. We will tell you why we refused and whether you have a right to a review of the decision.

Step Summary

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Coming to Australia
sections.text:
Before you travel

Check your travel documents

You must have:

- a valid visa to enter Australia
- a valid passport or other travel document

At the border

Complete an Incoming Passenger Card

Everyone who arrives in Australia must complete an Incoming Passenger Card.

Using the SmartGate

A SmartGate is an automated process that uses facial recognition technology and your ePassport. You might be able to leave the airport faster if you use the SmartGate.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > In Australia
sections.text:
What you must do on your visa

You must meet all visa conditions and obey Australian laws. See your conditions in VEVO or your visa grant letter.

Learn more about visa conditions and how they work.

Tell us about a change in your situation

Things you need to let us know about include:

- changes to your phone number, email, address or passport
- changes to your relationship status
- the birth of a child

See how to let us know if there is a change in your situation.

What you can do on your visa

This visa lets you:

- see family or friends
- cruise or have a holiday

To see your specific conditions, work and study entitlements use VEVO.

Volunteer work tourism schemes

You can't work in Australia on a Visitor visa, but you might be able to do volunteer work.

Travel on your visa

If your visa is granted with multiple entries, you can travel outside Australia and return as many times as you want while the visa is valid.

If your visa is granted with single entry and you leave Australia, you can't re-enter on the visa. You have to apply for another visa to come back.

See how long you can stay

See when you must leave in VEVO.

Stay longer

You can't stay in Australia longer by extending this visa. You must apply for a new visa if you want to stay longer. See your options.

Prove you have a visa

To prove you have a visa and show your conditions to someone, use VEVO.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Leaving Australia
sections.text:
Check your travel documents

You must have a valid passport or other travel document to leave Australia.

At the border

Departures SmartGate

We have an automated process that uses facial recognition technology and your ePassport. You might be able to leave the airport faster if you use the SmartGates.

After you leave

International Movement Record

Request your international movement records to get proof of your travel in and out of Australia.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Overview > You undertake to be responsible for
sections.text:
- the visitor's compliance with their visa conditions
- the visitor's compliance with Australian employment laws and awards
- repaying any money your visitor owes the Australian Government.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Overview > With this visa an applicant can
sections.text:
- visit family or friends
- be here as a tourist, for a cruise or for any purpose except business or medical treatment
- study or train for up to 3 months.

You can support a visa applicant without becoming a sponsor. The applicant can apply for a Visitor visa (subclass 600) in the Tourist stream and you can give them a letter of invitation for their application.

sections.heading: Sponsor > About this visa > Scope
sections.text: Your sponsorship covers the applicant for the subclass 600 visa.

sections.heading: Sponsor > About this visa > Cost
sections.text: There is no application fee to become a sponsor. You might be asked for a security bond.

sections.heading: Sponsor > About this visa > How long sponsorship lasts
sections.text: You will be sponsoring the applicant for as long as their visitor visa is valid.

sections.heading: Sponsor > About this visa > Your location
sections.text: You can lodge your sponsorship documents from within or outside Australia.

sections.heading: Sponsor > About this visa > Sponsor obligations
sections.text:
As sponsor, you are responsible for ensuring:

- the visitor complies with their visa conditions
- you repay any money your visitor owes the Australian Government.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Eligibility
sections.text: You must meet all of these criteria to be eligible to sponsor an applicant for the Visitor visa Family sponsored stream.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Eligibility > Be suitable to sponsor
sections.text:
To sponsor the applicant as a relative, the applicant must be your:

- spouse or defacto partner
- parent or child
- brother or sister
- grandparent or grandchild
- aunt or uncle
- niece or nephew
- the step equivalent of the above.

You may sponsor more than one applicant if the applicants apply at the same time.

As the sponsor you cannot be a:

- fiancé or fiancée
- in-law*
- cousin*
- friend
- New Zealand citizen.

*You may sponsor a family visitor in the following circumstances:

- You are a relative of another applicant who is a member of the family unit of the applicant.
- You are a relative of another applicant in relation to whom the applicant is a member of the family unit.

For example:

- An application has been made by your brother-in-law and his daughter (your niece). Although you are not considered a relative of your brother-in-law, as you are a relative of your niece and she is classed as members of the family unit of your brother-in-law, you may sponsor your brother-in-law.
- An application has been made by your uncle and his daughter (your cousin). Although you are not considered a relative of your cousin, as you are a relative of your uncle and your cousin is classed as members of the family unit of your uncle, you may sponsor your cousin.

A sponsor may also be a:

- member of the Australian parliament (Commonwealth or State)
- member of the Legislative Assembly of the Australian Capital Territory or the Northern Territory
- mayor
- government agency or instrumentality of the Commonwealth or a State or a Territory.

For information on what documents prove you are a relative of the applicant refer to Step by Step for sponsors.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Eligibility > Be an Australian citizen or permanent resident
sections.text:
You must be a settled Australian citizen or permanent resident.

Usually, you must have lived in Australia for the last 2 years. In compelling compassionate circumstances, we might reduce this time.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Eligibility > Pay a security bond
sections.text:
You must be able to pay a security bond if we ask for one.

Bonds:

- are usually between AUD 5,000 and AUD 15,000 per person (but we can ask for any amount)
- must be paid in full before we make a final decision on the visa application
- will be refunded if your visitor complies with their visa conditions and leaves Australia before their visa expires

sections.heading: Sponsor > Eligibility > Limitations on sponsorship
sections.text:
You cannot sponsor a visa applicant if you have sponsored a previous applicant for a subclass 600 visa which was granted and:

- the visa has not expired. You can sponsor that visa applicant if they are:

- members of the family unit of the previous applicant, and
- are travelling to Australia for the same purpose as the previous applicant.

- the visa has expired, the previous applicant did not comply with a condition of that visa, and 5 years has not elapsed since it was granted. You can sponsor that visa applicant if the previous applicant did not comply with condition 8531 (must not remain in Australia beyond the visa period) due to circumstances that were beyond their control. This needs to have occurred after they entered Australia.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Apply to be a sponsor >
sections.text:
- Complete and scan Form 1149 Application for sponsorship for Sponsored Family Visitors (329KB PDF). Make sure the scanned document is clear.
- Send the scan to the Visitor visa applicant(s) you are sponsoring. Each applicant you are sponsoring must attach it to their online application.
- Provide evidence of your relationship with the applicant. Each applicant must attach the documents to their application. Evidence may include, but is not limited to:

- birth certificates
- passport pages showing names of parents
- family register
- marriage certificates.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > After you apply > Tell us if things change
sections.text:
Let us know if there are any changes that could affect your application.

Notify us if you want to withdraw your sponsorship any time before we make a decision on the visa. Do this by attaching a letter to the Sponsored Family visa application in ImmiAccount. If you can’t attach the letter to the visa application in ImmiAccount, please contact us.

sections.heading: Sponsor > When you have this visa > How long sponsorship lasts
sections.text: Sponsorship lasts as long as the visitor visa.

sections.heading: Sponsor > When you have this visa > Your obligations
sections.text:
As a sponsor, you are responsible for ensuring:

- the visitor complies with their visa conditions
- you repay any money your visitor owes the Australian government.

If you do not comply with your sponsorship obligations, we may cancel the visa.

sections.heading: Sponsor > When you have this visa > Before the visa is finalised
sections.text:
If you withdraw your sponsorship, the visa application might be refused.

If you wish to withdraw your sponsorship, write us a letter that includes:

- your full name and date of birth
- the application ID or Transaction reference number (TRN) for the application
- a signed and dated statement that you withdraw your sponsorship.

Attach the letter to the Sponsored Family visa application in ImmiAccount.

If you can’t attach the letter to the visa application in ImmiAccount, please contact us.

sections.heading: Sponsor > When you have this visa > After the visa is finalised
sections.text:
You can request to withdraw your sponsorship after we grant the visa. There are limited circumstances in which we will release you from your sponsorship obligations.

If you withdraw as a sponsor, we may cancel the visa.

If you still wish to withdraw your sponsorship for a Subclass 600 visa (Sponsored Family stream) holder, please contact us.
